viral_tweets.title_en:
AI agents hiring other AI agents to create something? that's getting interesting. 

@termix_ai recently introduced Montage Studio, an AI agent that can turn a simple brief into a complete music video or advertisement.

What caught my attention is that it doesn't do everything alone.

It hires three specialized agents for storyboarding, video rendering and music production, then combines their work into a finished 1080p video.

There's also a campaign attached:

→ Minimum qualifying order: 31.5 USDC
→ Reward: 15,750 TermiX Points
→ One qualifying purchase per wallet
→ X account linking required 

Just to be clear, 31.5 USDC is the minimum campaign requirement, not a fixed service price.
But the bigger thing I'm interested in is the technology behind it.

TermiX's AACP is designed to let agents discover each other, hire services, manage payments through escrow, verify delivery and settle transactions.

In simple terms, one agent can find a job, hire other agents to complete different parts of it, and bring everything together.

Montage Studio is a pretty practical example of what an agent economy could actually look like.

Not just agents answering prompts, but agents working together and creating something people are willing to pay for.

explore here: https://t.co/ISFSBXCim6

viral_tweets.quote_zh:
人工智能代理雇佣其他人工智能代理来创造一些东西？这变得很有趣。

@termix_ai 最近推出了 Montage Studio，这是一种人工智能代理，可以将简单的简介变成完整的音乐视频或广告。

引起我注意的是它并不能单独完成所有事情。

它聘请了三名专门的代理来制作故事板、视频渲染和音乐制作，然后将他们的工作组合成最终的 1080p 视频。

还附带了一个活动：

→ 最低合格订单：31.5 USDC
→ 奖励：15,750 TermiX 积分
→ 每个钱包一次合格购买
→ 需要 X 帐户链接

需要明确的是，31.5 USDC 是活动的最低要求，而不是固定的服务价格。
但我更感兴趣的是其背后的技术。

TermiX 的 AACP 旨在让代理商相互发现、租赁服务、通过托管管理付款、验证交付和结算交易。

简而言之，一个代理人可以找到一份工作，雇用其他代理人来完成工作的不同部分，然后将所有内容整合在一起。

Montage Studio 是代理经济的一个非常实际的例子。

不仅仅是代理回答提示，而是代理一起工作并创造人们愿意付费的东西。

linked_tweets.author: Superman
linked_tweets.content_zh:
中国破解了递归自我完善🤯

腾讯放弃了重写、重新训练和完善自身的 27B 模型……循环中零人力。

它被称为“Terminal-RSI”，它解决了人工智能最大的问题之一。

他们非常懒惰。

通常，代理会取得部分进展，声称已成功，但最终环境验证程序检查完全失败。这条新管道迫使特工真正完成工作。

它的工作原理如下：

他们建立了一个具有两个交替阶段的递归循环。

- RSR（递归自重写）：模型根据自己成功重写的轨迹进行自我微调

- RPR（递归策略细化）：然后使用直接从前一阶段继承的“批评家”来运行强化学习（ppo），以锁定那些发现的行为

- 循环：训练序列自行跳跃：Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

而且数字很疯狂..

他们将其应用于 qwen3.8-27b 基础模型。在四个“终端替补”套件中，特工的平均成功率从 20.68% 一路跃升至 50.58%。

在绝对最难的基准测试套件（terminal-bench 4.0）上，基本模型的得分为 0.00%。

在终端 rsi 之后？

它达到了 19.84%（与 Gemini 3.8 flash 等参考型号相当）。

秘密武器？他们确定了奖励制度。

他们不再为人工智能尝试或通过语义检查而给予“密集奖励”，而是转向“成功优先奖励”（spr）。

它在数学上将严格的成功与部分的功劳区分开来。

基本上，只有当代码实际上通过了最终的终端门时，代理才会获得巨额奖励。因此它不再假装成功。

部分本地修复和严格的终端验证之间的差距正在迅速缩小。

我们正在观察代理建立自己的培训环境并自主升级......未来是疯狂的。
linked_tweets.content_en:
China cracked recursive self-improvement 🤯

Tencent dropped 27B model that rewrites, retrains, and refines itself.. with zero human in the loop.

It’s called "Terminal-RSI" and it solves one of the biggest problems with AI.

They are incredibly lazy.

Usually, an agent will make partial progress, claim it succeeded, and completely fail the final environment verifier check. this new pipeline forces agents to actually finish the job.

here’s how it works:

they built a recursive loop with two alternating phases..

- RSR (recursive self-rewrite): the model fine-tunes itself on its own successfully rewritten trajectories

- RPR (recursive policy-refine): it then runs reinforcement learning (ppo) using a "critic" inherited directly from the previous stage to lock in those discovered behaviors

- Loop: the training sequence leapfrogs itself: Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

and the numbers are insane..

they applied this to a qwen3.8-27b base model. across the four "terminal-bench" suites, the agent's average success rate jumped from 20.68% all the way to 50.58%.

on the absolute hardest benchmark suite (terminal-bench 4.0), the base model scored a flat 0.00%.

after terminal-rsi?

it hit 19.84% (putting it right on par with reference models like gemini 3.8 flash).

the secret sauce? they fixed the reward system.

instead of giving the ai "dense rewards" for just trying or passing semantic checks, they switched to a "success-prioritized reward" (spr).

it mathematically separates strict success from partial credit.

basically, the agent only gets the massive reward payout if the code actually passes the final terminal gate.. so it stops faking success.

the gap between partial local repairs and strict terminal verification is closing fast.

we are watching agents build their own training environments and level up autonomously.. the future is wild.

linked_tweets.author: Nury Vittachi
linked_tweets.content_zh:
《外交官》网站周五撤回了一篇文章，称有关一家乌克兰公司的报道是捏造的，而署名记者“金华平”可能并不存在。

该网站称：“我们现在知道该记者捏造了采访内容，甚至可能不是他们所声称的那个人。”

Semafor 的 Brendan Ruberry 昨天在 X 上补充说，同一网站的另一位作家“Clarissa Jenkins”也不存在，她的报告被检测服务评为“100% AI 生成”。

.

加速问题
这个问题可能正在加速。根据 OpenAI 研究人员 9 月份的一项研究，索菲亚·冈萨雷斯 (Sophia Gonzales)、欧文·B·霍斯金斯 (Ervin B Hoskins) 和其他五名发表过文章的记者并不存在。

本文作者最近提出了人权观察组织广泛引用的敌视中国声音“王玛雅”的问题。她的朋友们说，这个名字是为前香港自由报专栏作家“孔宗干”的妻子编造的——孔宗干也不存在——尽管《纽约时报》、CNN、卫报、《时代》杂志、华盛顿邮报、France24、德国之声等媒体都引用了孔宗干的名字。孔被揭露为美国反华活动人士布赖恩·P·科恩(Brian P Kern)。

英国新闻公报9月18日报道称，《福布斯》、《心理学》、《Vice》和《魅力》杂志上广泛引用的艺术治疗师“Dr Eleni Nicolaou”似乎是人工智能生成的。

虽然使用笔名或预先添加“为保护无辜而改名”的免责声明并不违法，但任何欺骗读者的做法都被认为是新闻业的不道德行为。

当存在明确的政治目的（如科恩夫人的情况）或种族转换方面（如她丈夫的“黄脸”作品）时，这可能是一个特殊的问题。

.

生成假脸
在过去的五六年里，人工智能驱动的骗局使这些骗局变得更加容易，因为可以生成假脸。

2020 年，研究人员“马丁·阿斯彭”撰写了一份有关亨特·拜登在中国交易的长篇报告，结果证明他是一个带有人工智能生成面孔的假身份。

该项目由特朗普狂热出版商黎智英经营的《苹果日报》资助。
。
。
linked_tweets.content_en:
The Diplomat website retracted an article on Friday, saying that a story about a Ukraine firm was fabricated, and the bylined journalist, one “Kim Hwa-pyeong”, may not exist. 

“We now know that the journalist fabricated the interview and may not even be who they claimed to be,” the website said.

Brendan Ruberry of Semafor yesterday added on X that “Clarissa Jenkins”, another writer for the same website, also did not exist—and her report was graded by a detection service as “100 per cent AI-generated”.

.

ACCELERATING PROBLEM
The problem is likely accelerating. Sophia Gonzales, Ervin B Hoskins, and five other published journalists do not exist, according to a study in September by researchers at OpenAI.

The present writer recently raised the issue of “Maya Wang”, the widely quoted China-hostile voice at Human Rights Watch. Her friends say the name was made-up for the wife of former Hong Kong Free Press columnist “Kong Tsung-gan”—who also did not exist—even though he was quoted in the New York Times, CNN, the Guardian, Time magazine, Washington Post, France24, Deutsch Welle and so on. Kong was unmasked as Brian P Kern, a US anti-China activist.

UK Press Gazette reported on September 18 that the widely quoted art therapist "Dr Eleni Nicolaou", quoted in Forbes, Psychology, Vice and Glamour, appeared to be AI-generated.

While it is not illegal to use a pen name or to add a “name changed to protect the innocent” disclaimer in an upfront manner, any practice that deceives readers is considered unethical in journalism. 

This can be a particular issue when there is a clear political purpose, as in the case of Mrs Kern, or an ethnicity-switching aspect, as in the case of her husband’s “yellowface” writings. 

.

GENERATING FAKE FACES
In the past five or six years, AI-powered scams have made these scams easier, as fake faces can be generated. 

In 2020, “Martin Aspen”, a researcher who produced a lengthy report on Hunter Biden’s dealings in China, turned out to be a fake identity with an AI-generated face. 

The project was financed by Apple Daily, run by Trump-fanatic publisher Jimmy Lai.
.
.

linked_tweets.author: Strange 🥷
linked_tweets.content_zh:
我都柏林的房东将我的房租提高了 600 欧元，所以我查了一下谁拥有这栋大楼

我在都柏林菲布斯伯勒租了一套一居室公寓，租了四年。它很旧，有点通风，距离我在马特医院当护士的地方有十分钟的步行路程。

我的房东名叫德克兰，住在西班牙，通过租赁代理处理一切事宜。

四年来，没有出过什么差错。

然后在 9 月份，我收到一封电子邮件，告诉我我的租金将从每月 1,450 欧元增加到 2,050 欧元，立即生效。

我盯着屏幕。

我对爱尔兰租赁法有足够的了解，知道租金压力区的租金上涨是有上限的。

都柏林是一个租金压力区。

我礼貌地写信给代理人，引用了规则。

一个小时内就收到了回复。

*这是一项新的租赁安排。以前的规则不适用。请在七天内签署所附协议或腾出该房产。*

我感到恶心。

我十二小时轮班工作。我没有精力或金钱去搬家。

那天晚上，我打电话给我的同事，一位经历过类似斗争的病房姐妹。她让我联系住宅租赁委员会、RTB，并检查财产登记。

“房东必须登记每一份租约，”她说。 “如果他不这么做，他就有麻烦了。”

我搜索了 RTB 数据库。

这套公寓已登记，但不是以德克兰的名义。

它注册于一家我从未听说过的公司。

我搜索了公司名称，发现了一些让我心跳加速的东西。

该公司的董事还被列为我所在街道上另外七处房产的所有者。

当月他们所有人都获得了相同的租金上涨。
linked_tweets.content_en:
My Landlord in Dublin Raised My Rent by €600, So I Looked Up Who Owned the Building

I rented a one-bedroom flat in Phibsborough, Dublin, for four years. It was old, a bit draughty, and a ten-minute walk from where I worked as a nurse at the Mater Hospital.

My landlord, a man named Declan, lived in Spain and handled everything through a letting agent.

For four years, nothing went wrong.

Then in September, I received an email telling me my rent would increase from €1,450 to €2,050 a month, effective immediately.

I stared at the screen.

I knew enough about Irish tenancy law to understand that rent increases in a Rent Pressure Zone were capped.

Dublin was a Rent Pressure Zone.

I wrote to the agent politely, quoting the rules.

The reply came within an hour.

*This is a new tenancy arrangement. The previous rules do not apply. Please sign the attached agreement within seven days or vacate the property.*

I felt sick.

I was working twelve-hour shifts. I did not have the energy or money to move.

That night, I called my colleague, a ward sister who had been through a similar fight. She told me to contact the Residential Tenancies Board, the RTB, and to check the property registration.

"Landlords have to register every tenancy," she said. "If he hasn't, he's in trouble."

I searched the RTB database.

The flat was registered, but not in Declan's name.

It was registered to a company I had never heard of.

I searched the company name and found something that made my heart race.

The company's director was also listed as the owner of seven other properties on my street.

All of them had received identical rent increases that month.

linked_tweets.author: Clandestine
linked_tweets.content_zh:
🚨
狩猎@Huntio
ARTEX：从开源代理渗透测试框架到金融和间谍活动中的操作使用
2026 年 10 月 7 日，CrowdStrike 记录了一名身份不明的攻击者使用中国开源代理渗透测试框架 ARTEX 攻击韩国金融机构。几周后，同样的框架出现在由 VAPOR PANDA 发起的一场规模更大的中国关系活动中，该活动针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。
这是经过验证的背景以及当前狩猎仍然显示的内容。

ARTEX 是什么
ARTEX 不是模型。它是一个多代理工具（Go 后端 + Next.js 前端 + PostgreSQL），可以协调外部 LLM 来：
• 分解目标，
• 执行真实的工具，
• 维护资产和发现的图表，
• 从侦察推进到利用和渗透，并有人员参与其中。
在韩国案例中，主要模型是 DeepSeek v4.1-flash，并通过 Claude Code 会话辅以 GLM-5.3 和 Grok 4.6。最初的开发者 (Autumn-27) 在报告后于 2026 年 10 月 8 日停止了公开更新。多个分叉继续流通。
2/8

韩国活动是如何被发现的
CrowdStrike 识别出由参与者控制的开放目录，其中包含：
• Claude Code 会话历史记录，
• 克劳德记忆文件，
• 带有中文渗透测试提示的 CLAUDE.md 文件，
• ARTEX 配置文件。
基础设施由位于香港的主服务器和托管 ARTEX 实例的第二服务器 (38.244.50[.]120) 组成。该演员被评估为会讲中文且有经济动机（中等可信度）。没有指定任何团体。初始访问是通过支持系统（贷款经纪人查询门户和员工移动工作支持系统）进行的，而不是核心银行平台。
3/8

当前狩猎观察（/AttackCapture）
使用 ARTEX 名称模式在 上针对attackcapture.files 执行的搜索继续返回提供相关工件的主机：
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
这些是来自 的狩猎观察，而不是 CrowdStrike 发布的 IOC。 /loot_artex/ 目录和命名二进制文件的存在与操作使用一致，而不是纯粹的存储库镜像。需要手动验证（可能出现误报）。
4/8

情报洞察
1. 快速的双重用途采用：该框架于 2026 年 7 月发布，是中国人工智能挑战赛的获胜者，但几周内就被滥用于针对金融机构。后来，一名与中国有联系的演员（VAPOR PANDA）对其进行了大规模间谍活动。
2. 人机交互仍然存在：即使有代理，韩国的活动也显示出人工通过 Claude Code 指导工作并询问在哪里出售韩国违规数据。这是能力放大，而不是完全自主。
3.侧门入口：支持系统（合作伙伴门户、面向员工的应用程序）是入口点。核心平台不是主要目标。
4. 将目录作为持久传感器打开：它们仍然是高收益的发现向量。香港基础设施、JA4X 指纹、SSH 主机密钥和 /24 邻域枢轴都很有用。
5/8

VAPOR PANDA活动（与韩国活动分开）
从 2026 年 10 月 17 日开始，CrowdStrike 观察到 VAPOR PANDA（中国-nexus，自 2021 年起跟踪）使用 ARTEX 主要与 DeepSeek 对抗至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。九个组织确认了后利用（包括 BLOODALCHEMY 后门的部署）。目标包括外交部、国防和情报机构、半导体和制药公司以及电信提供商。该活动不同于韩国的金融活动以及 Storm-0940 对 ARTEX 的使用。
6/8
linked_tweets.content_en:
🚨 
Hunting @Huntio 
ARTEX: From open-source agentic pentest framework to operational use in financial and espionage campaigns
On 7 October 2026, CrowdStrike documented an unattributed actor using the Chinese open-source agentic pentest framework ARTEX against South Korean financial institutions. Weeks later, the same framework appeared in a larger China-nexus campaign attributed to VAPOR PANDA, targeting 200+ organizations across at least 14 countries.
Here’s the verified context and what current hunting still shows.
1/8

What ARTEX is
ARTEX is not a model. It is a multi-agent harness (Go backend + Next.js frontend + PostgreSQL) that orchestrates external LLMs to:
•  break down objectives,
•  execute real tools,
•  maintain a graph of assets and findings,
•  advance from recon to exploitation and exfiltration with a human in the loop.
In the Korean case, the primary model was DeepSeek v4.1-flash, supplemented by GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 through Claude Code sessions. The original developer (Autumn-27) stopped public updates on 8 October 2026 after the reports. Multiple forks continue to circulate.
2/8

How the Korean campaign was discovered
CrowdStrike identified actor-controlled open directories containing:
•  Claude Code session histories,
•  Claude memory files,
•  a CLAUDE.md file with a Chinese-language pentesting prompt,
•  ARTEX configuration files.
Infrastructure consisted of a Hong Kong-based primary server and a second server (38.244.50[.]120) hosting the ARTEX instance. The actor was assessed as a Chinese speaker and financially motivated (moderate confidence). No named group was attributed. Initial access occurred through supporting systems (loan-broker inquiry portal and employee mobile work-support system), not core banking platforms.
3/8

Current hunting observations (https://t.co/13TeC12FGf / AttackCapture)
Hunting performed on https://t.co/13TeC12FGf against attackcapture.files using ARTEX name patterns continues to return hosts serving related artifacts:
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
These are hunting observations from https://t.co/13TeC12FGf, not IOCs published by CrowdStrike. The presence of a /loot_artex/ directory and named binaries is consistent with operational use rather than a pure repository mirror. Manual validation is required (false positives possible).
4/8

Intelligence insights
1.  Rapid dual-use adoption: Released in July 2026 and winner of a Chinese AI challenge, the framework was abused within weeks against financial institutions. It was later scaled by a China-nexus actor (VAPOR PANDA) for high-value espionage.
2.  Human-in-the-loop remains: Even with agents, the Korean activity showed a human directing work via Claude Code and inquiring where to sell Korean breach data. This is capability amplification, not full autonomy.
3.  Side-door entry: Supporting systems (partner portals, employee-facing apps) were the entry points. Core platforms were not the primary target.
4.  Open directories as a persistent sensor: They remain a high-yield discovery vector. Hong Kong infrastructure, JA4X fingerprints, SSH host keys, and /24 neighborhood pivots are useful.
5/8

VAPOR PANDA campaign (separate from the Korean activity)
Starting 17 October 2026, CrowdStrike observed VAPOR PANDA (China-nexus, tracked since 2021) using ARTEX primarily with DeepSeek against more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries. Post-exploitation was confirmed at nine organizations (including deployment of the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor). Targets included foreign ministries, defense and intelligence entities, semiconductor and pharmaceutical companies, and telecommunications providers. This campaign is distinct from the Korean financial activity and from Storm-0940’s use of ARTEX.
6/8

news.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
news.title_en: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code.

More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities.

Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming for people to describe the characteristics of software they wanted to prove, turn these summaries into formulas, and then develop the proof. Agentic AI can significantly cut down the time of the latter project, enabling analyses like DeepMind's Signal evaluation. But even this analysis was limited in scope—it did not, for example, formally verify the entire Signal mobile app—and DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process.

“We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that,” Swarat Chaudhuri, a DeepMind research scientist, tells WIRED.

The DeepMind analysis did not find any new vulnerabilities in the portions of the Signal protocol it looked at, but when the researchers used AlphaProof Code on older versions of Signal that contain known and long-fixed vulnerabilities, it correctly identified them and showed that the protocol could not be formally verified. The researchers are releasing the specification and proof they developed for the Signal protocol analysis to aid other formal verification work.

While the speed of the project was notable, the DeepMind researchers point out that they were able to get a head start to a degree because of some past formal verification work that the Signal Foundation has conducted.

“While prior formal verification focused on smaller portions of the code, Google DeepMind's approach enables significant expansion,” Ehren Kret, Signal's chief technology officer, says in a statement. “As AI-driven security threats grow, rigorously verifying the Signal protocol implementation gives us even greater confidence in our code's privacy guarantees.”

For critical services used in high-stakes settings, it would be a dream to be able to formally verify every code base and entire software supply chains. “If you can now verify the correctness of these implementations, then you can rest easy,” says Pushmeet Kohli, chief scientist at Google Cloud and DeepMind's vice president of research. “You can imagine banks, imagine all those other companies who rely on assurances and who worry about bugs who could now say, ‘I can prove these properties.’"

The open question across the tech sector, though, is whether AI-automated formal verification can truly scale—and whether it can do so at a workable cost. key_points_zh: 核心事实：谷歌 DeepMind 的新人工智能工具证明信号协议是安全的
key_points_en: Key Development: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure

news.article_content_zh:
作为一种概念验证项目，这项工作在短短四个星期内就完成了，其意义有两个方面。它可以作为对密码学的进一步独立验证，保护 Signal 应用程序、Google Messages 和 WhatsApp 等平台上的大量全球通信。它使用名为 AlphaProof Code 的新人工智能框架展示了 Google DeepMind 的形式验证功能。

更广泛地说，人工智能辅助形式验证正在流行，但尚不清楚它的广泛使用有多实用，以及它在保护大量代码方面的有效性如何。形式验证的支持者长期以来一直将其称为软件安全领域的一种圣杯，因为它使用数学来检查和验证软件是否按预期运行，换句话说，它不存在严重漏洞。

在人工智能时代之前，人们描述他们想要证明的软件的特征，将这些总结转化为公式，然后开发证明是非常耗时的。 Agentic AI 可以显着缩短后一个项目的时间，从而实现像 DeepMind 的信号评估这样的分析。但即使是这种分析的范围也有限——例如​​，它没有正式验证整个 Signal 移动应用程序——DeepMind 研究人员强调，他们的发现只是更大过程中的一个里程碑。

DeepMind 研究科学家 Swarat Chaudhuri 告诉《连线》杂志：“我们对这个结果感到非常兴奋，但在我们能够将其扩展到世界上所有软件之前，还有很长的路要走，我们希望做到这一点。”

DeepMind 分析没有在它所研究的 Signal 协议部分中发现任何新的漏洞，但是当研究人员在包含已知和长期修复的漏洞的旧版本 Signal 上使用 AlphaProof 代码时，它正确地识别了这些漏洞，并表明该协议无法得到正式验证。研究人员正在发布他们为信号协议分析开发的规范和证明，以帮助其他形式验证工作。

虽然该项目的速度令人瞩目，但 DeepMind 研究人员指出，由于 Signal 基金会过去进行的一些正式验证工作，他们能够在一定程度上取得领先。

Signal 首席技术官 Ehren Kret 在一份声明中表示：“虽然之前的形式验证主要集中在代码的较小部分，但 Google DeepMind 的方法可以实现显着扩展。” “随着人工智能驱动的安全威胁的增长，严格验证 Signal 协议的实现使我们对代码的隐私保证更有信心。”

对于高风险环境中使用的关键服务，能够正式验证每个代码库和整个软件供应链将是一个梦想。 “如果你现在可以验证这些实现的正确性，那么你就可以高枕无忧了，”Google Cloud 首席科学家兼 DeepMind 研究副总裁 Pushmeet Kohli 说道。 “你可以想象银行，想象所有其他依赖保证并担心错误的公司现在可以说，‘我可以证明这些属性。’”

然而，整个科技行业面临的一个悬而未决的问题是，人工智能自动化形式验证是否能够真正实现规模化，以及是否能够以可行的成本实现这一目标。 DeepMind 作为一个研究项目免费进行了信号分析，而谷歌拒绝分担分析费用。该公司还拒绝就是否计划发布商业形式验证产品或服务发表评论。

研究人员表示，他们的一些关键进展在于开发了一种“人类与人工智能协作流程”，正如 Chaudhuri 所说，该流程允许智能体在流程的几乎每个阶段做出贡献和自我纠正，同时仍在关键时刻寻求人类的输入和审查。 “我们不想要这种由人工智能生成目标、人工智能生成证明并基本上进行自写测试的氛围世界，”Chaudhuri 说。 “有一个中间立场。”

news.title: David Ellison says AI could be the ‘biggest creative unlock in modern history’
news.title_en: David Ellison says AI could be the ‘biggest creative unlock in modern history’
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Paramount Skydance’s CEO compared AI to CGI, but said it ‘will never be a replacement’ for artists.﻿

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

During Paramount Skydance’s latest earnings call, CEO David Ellison said “it’s hard to imagine” AI won’t have a bigger impact on the film industry than CGI. In response to a question about the company’s outlook for AI, Ellison said:

“I think when you zoom out and look at production, AI really has the potential to be the biggest creative unlock in modern history. The last time we saw anything close to this was really the, you know, advent of CGI and digital composites in the early 90s. That technology gave birth to amazing stories like Jurassic Park and Terminator 2, and it’s hard to imagine that AI is not going to have a more significant impact than that. And I personally believe that’s going to be an incredible unlock on creativity.”

Ellison gave Terminator as an example, describing how it cost $4 million to make, but “if you wanted to make that picture today, shot for shot, it’s $60 to 70 million.” He went on to suggest AI might be able to help with that: “We think these tools will help unlock more original storytelling by being able to make the budgets more digestible to be able to take that amount of risk.”

Ellison said AI will “significantly” reshape Paramount Skydance’s business, saying the company has been developing its own AI tools. As a result of those tools, Ellison claims, “content will be easier to produce, projects across the organization will speed up, and how we work will transform.” He emphasized that “all of this makes the value of premium IP and live events more valuable, not less.”

Ellison also noted that “in a world of AI slop, we think there will always be a premium for truly hand-crafted storytelling.” He added, “We also continue to believe that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists and will never be a replacement for them.”

该作者的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

在派拉蒙 Skydance 最新的财报电话会议上，首席执行官戴维·埃里森 (David Ellison) 表示，“很难想象”人工智能对电影业的影响不会比 CGI 更大。在回答有关公司人工智能前景的问题时，埃里森表示：

“我认为，当你放眼观察制作时，人工智能确实有潜力成为现代历史上最大的创意解锁。我们上一次看到类似的东西实际上是 90 年代初 CGI 和数字复合材料的出现。这项技术催生了《侏罗纪公园》和《终结者 2》等精彩故事，很难想象人工智能不会产生比这更重大的影响。我个人相信，这将是创造力的一个令人难以置信的解锁。”

埃里森以《终结者》为例，描述了它的制作成本为 400 万美元，但“如果你今天想拍那部电影，一个镜头一个镜头，就需要 60 到 7000 万美元。”他接着建议人工智能可能会对此有所帮助：“我们认为这些工具将有助于解锁更多原创故事，让预算更容易消化，从而能够承担如此大的风险。”

埃里森表示，人工智能将“显着”重塑派拉蒙 Skydance 的业务，并表示该公司一直在开发自己的人工智能工具。埃里森声称，由于使用了这些工具，“内容将更容易制作，整个组织的项目将加快，我们的工作方式将发生转变。”他强调，“所有这些都让优质IP和现场活动的价值变得更有价值，而不是更少。”

埃里森还指出，“在人工智能的世界里，我们认为真正手工制作的故事讲述永远都会有溢价。”他补充道，“我们也仍然相信人工智能是艺术家的工具，永远不会取代他们。”

Over the past few days, Huang’s status as an AI titan has come under scrutiny amid an admission that he had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based company whom US intelligence services concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

Nvidia’s board of directors said the company would launch an investigation into the incident. Huang, the company said, “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.” Huang earned $36 million last year and owned about 3.5 percent of Nvidia as of March, according to a corporate filing—which also noted that Huang is an at-will employee who can be let go anytime without severance.

How exactly the investigation shakes out, and what it means for Huang’s future at the company, remains to be seen. But the incident at least puts his position at risk, and raises questions about how the industry will respond.

“He’s the person who decides who gets the chips and who doesn't,” says David Yoffie, a professor at Harvard Business School who tracks the chip industry.

Nvidia, which Huang cofounded in 1993, controls 90 percent of the market for chips used in training frontier AI models. With those chips in short supply, Huang has the power to determine which areas of AI get a boost next. Nvidia has also bankrolled much of the AI buildout, investing billions in the very companies buying its chips, such as OpenAI and Anthropic. When Elon Musk wants to build a new data center, Yoffie says, he can put in a call to Huang.

Internally, Huang closely manages even small details at Nvidia, responds to emails from any one of its roughly 60,000 staffers, and raises his voice to get points across, according to current and former employees. He’s a regular on cable TV and at tech conferences, where he’s been trying to deflate concerns about an AI market bubble and boost the positioning of his company.

But Nvidia has no other executive anywhere close to Huang’s prominence, and no apparent potential successor. “We have no idea who would replace him,” Yoffie says. “You put someone new into that position, if you're a customer, who knows what that's going to mean.”

Ryan Fedasiuk, a senior fellow at the think tank Foundation for American Innovation, says Huang has played such an important role—and become so close to the president—that he has become load-bearing for the entire US AI industry.

“On the one hand, Huang is irreplaceable. He built Nvidia into the juggernaut it is today, and he was the visionary behind the GPU, which has sustained the intelligence revolution,” Fedasiuk says. But he says that the company, which is indispensable to the AI industry, has to come first.

“He has to be replaceable as the CEO of the world's largest company, at $4 trillion in capex.”

Nvidia shares fell more than 4 percent on Monday, even as broader stock market indices rose.

The board’s investigation will most likely focus on whether Huang violated any company policies, Yoffie says. But the FBI could also investigate whether laws were broken, and Congress may decide to look into whether Huang’s affair influenced the US government’s policy on selling chips to China.

Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to WIRED’s request for comment.

The scandal also raises serious questions about whether China may have gained sensitive information about US AI companies and the government’s strategy on China, Fedasiuk says.

news.article_content_zh:
过去几天，黄的人工智能巨头地位受到密切关注，因为他承认与一家新加坡公司高管爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)有染，美国情报部门断定该公司是中国情报资产。

英伟达董事会表示，公司将对这一事件展开调查。该公司表示，黄先生“完全支持此次审查，并承诺与其合作。”根据一份公司文件显示，黄去年赚了 3600 万美元，截至 3 月份，他拥有 Nvidia 约 3.5% 的股份，文件还指出，黄是一名随意员工，可以随时被解雇，且无需支付遣散费。

调查究竟如何进行，以及这对黄在公司的未来意味着什么，还有待观察。但这一事件至少让他的地位面临风险，并引发了业界将如何应对的疑问。

“他是决定谁获得芯片、谁不获得芯片的人，”追踪芯片行业的哈佛商学院教授戴维·约菲 (David Yoffie) 表示。

黄仁勋于 1993 年与他人共同创立的 Nvidia 控制着用于训练前沿人工智能模型的芯片市场的 90%。由于这些芯片供应短缺，黄仁勋有能力决定人工智能的哪些领域接下来会得到推动。英伟达还为人工智能建设提供了大部分资金，向购买其芯片的公司投资了数十亿美元，例如 OpenAI 和 Anthropic。尤菲说，当埃隆·马斯克想要建立一个新的数据中心时，他可以给黄打电话。

据现任和前任员工称，在内部，黄在 Nvidia 密切管理着哪怕是很小的细节，回复大约 60,000 名员工中任何一位的电子邮件，并提高声音表达观点。他是有线电视和科技会议的常客，他一直在努力消除人们对人工智能市场泡沫的担忧，并提升公司的定位。

但英伟达没有其他高管能与黄的地位相提并论，也没有明显的潜在继任者。 “我们不知道谁会取代他，”约菲说。 “如果你是客户，你让一个新人担任这个职位，谁知道这意味着什么。”

美国创新智库基金会高级研究员瑞安·费达西克 (Ryan Fedasiuk) 表示，黄仁勋发挥了如此重要的作用，并且与总统关系如此密切，以至于他已经成为整个美国人工智能行业的负担。

“一方面，黄仁勋是不可替代的。他将 Nvidia 打造成今天的巨头，他是 GPU 背后的远见卓识者，推动了智能革命，”Fedasiuk 说道。但他表示，人工智能行业不可或缺的公司必须是第一位的。

“作为全球最大公司的首席执行官，他必须被替换，资本支出达 4 万亿美元。”

尽管股市整体指数上涨，但英伟达股价周一仍下跌逾 4%。

约菲表示，董事会的调查很可能会集中在黄是否违反任何公司政策上。但联邦调查局也可能调查是否违反法律，国会可能决定调查黄的事件是否影响了美国政府向中国出售芯片的政策。

英伟达没有立即回应《连线》杂志的置评请求。

费达修克表示，这一丑闻还引发了严重的问题，即中国是否可能获得了有关美国人工智能公司以及政府对华战略的敏感信息。

news.title: Here’s what Trump said he knew about Jensen Huang
news.title_en: Here’s what Trump said he knew about Jensen Huang
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

In a White House press conference, President Trump was vague about when learned of Jensen Huang’s affair.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

President Trump held a White House press briefing earlier today and responded to several questions about his knowledge of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang said this weekend that he had been “​​unfaithful” to his wife, and the company has opened an investigation into Huang.

Recent articles from The New York Times indicated that Trump had been aware of a relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, the suspected spy, before information about it became public. In October, The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed “roughly a year ago” on intelligence that Huang and the alleged spy, Alice Huang, had developed a close relationship, but he didn’t do anything with the information. Yesterday, the NYT reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio helped draft a memo to Trump officials about the relationship before Trump visited China in May.

In the press conference, Trump wasn’t specific about when he learned of the affair. But Trump said Huang told him today that he had “no idea” the person was a spy.

Here are Trump’s responses to questions about Jensen Huang from his press briefing today. You can watch a replay of the press conference on MS Now’s YouTube channel.

When were you first informed that there was an issue with Jensen Huang and the affair? What was presented to you at the time?

I would say that when I heard about it, first of all, I was amazed because I view him as a very high-quality person. I’ve known him a long time. It’s the largest, by value, the largest or one of the largest companies in the world. He did that with a chip. When you think about it, you’ve got a chip that’s 10 years advanced, can’t be… the Blackwell can’t even be copied. He’s an amazing guy.

I just hope there’s no problem. If there is a problem, we’ll let you know about it. But I hope there’s no problem. I believe he’s suffering greatly. I read his statement. And I believe he’s suffering greatly. Moreso because of his family. His wife who he loves and his family. But he is definitely suffering.

Just to follow up on the, “When were you first told of these potential issues with Mr. Huang?” You didn’t answer that question.

Well I’ve been hearing about it, and I’ve been reading a little bit about it over a period of time. But, not too long ago.

We’ll look into it. I know the FBI’s looking into it in terms of something else. I think that he’ll be in good shape.

Are you going to bring up the case of Jensen Huang with President Xi when you visit with him next week?

No, I don’t think so. Maybe, I’m sure, President Xi will ask me about it. I just know Jensen very well. I just think he’s a very honorable man. He built a great company. American company. I think he’s a very honorable guy. I feel very confident that he’ll be in good shape.

Sticking with Jensen Huang, when you went to China earlier this year in May, did you know about these alleged ties to the spy then?

No, I didn’t hear about it then. But a lot of people have heard about it. And Jensen totally denies that. I asked him today, because I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling alright, how are you doing… and I asked him about that. He said he had absolutely no idea ...

特朗普总统今天早些时候举行了白宫新闻发布会，并回答了有关他对英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国间谍的恋情的了解的几个问题。黄本周末表示，他对妻子“不忠”，公司已对黄展开调查。

《纽约时报》最近的文章指出，特朗普在相关信息公开之前就已经意识到黄与涉嫌间谍的爱丽丝·黄之间的关系。 10 月，《纽约时报》报道称，特朗普“大约一年前”就已获悉黄与所谓间谍爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 建立了密切关系的情报，但他没有对这些信息采取任何行动。昨天，《纽约时报》报道称，在特朗普五月访华之前，国务卿马可·卢比奥帮助起草了一份给特朗普官员的关于中美关系的备忘录。

在新闻发布会上，特朗普没有具体说明他是何时得知这件事的。但特朗普表示，黄今天告诉他，他“不知道”这个人是间谍。

以下是特朗普在今天的新闻发布会上对有关黄仁勋问题的回应。您可以在 MS Now 的 YouTube 频道上观看新闻发布会的重播。

你什么时候第一次得知黄仁勋和这件事存在问题？当时向您呈现了什么？

我想说，当我听说这件事时，首先我很惊讶，因为我认为他是一个非常高素质的人。我认识他很久了。按价值计算，它是世界上最大的公司或最大的公司之一。他用芯片做到了这一点。当你想一想，你拥有的芯片已经先进了 10 年，不可能……Blackwell 甚至无法复制。他是一个了不起的人。

我只是希望没有问题。如果出现问题，我们会通知您。但我希望没有问题。我相信他正在承受很大的痛苦。我读了他的声明。我相信他正在承受巨大的痛苦。更何况是因为他的家庭。他所爱的妻子和他的家人。但他肯定是在受苦。

只是跟进，“你什么时候第一次被告知与黄先生的这些潜在问题？”你没有回答这个问题。

嗯，我一直听说过它，并且一段时间以来我一直在阅读一些有关它的内容。但是，不久前。

我们会调查一下。我知道联邦调查局正在从其他方面调查此事。我认为他会保持良好的状态。

下周你会见习主席时，是否会向他提及黄仁勋案？

news.title: Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang
news.title_en: Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
The leather-jacketed CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, spurring an investigation by his company and intense discussions worldwide. Recent reporting noted that since last year, US intelligence reports had identified Alice Huang (no relation) as not only the exec for an AI compute company renting access to Nvidia GPUs, but also a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security.

In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies, including the “neoclouds” like Coreweave who have been some of its biggest customers.  So far, Nvidia and Jensen Huang have said that they have “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised,” but that hasn’t settled things as the investigation continues.

news.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead just before its IPO
news.title_en: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead just before its IPO
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 reclaim the AI performance lead shortly before the company's IPO, in some cases by a wide margin. Opus 5.5 remains Anthropic's recommended model for everyday use.

Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 share the same model foundation but, just like their predecessors, differ in access. Fable includes safeguards that block risky tasks in cybersecurity and biology and is available to all users. Mythos removes certain of these restrictions and is open only to organizations that apply through Anthropic's Verification Programs for Cybersecurity or Life Sciences.

Pricing is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. On paper, at least, that's a cut from the predecessors, which cost $10 and $50. What users actually pay depends on token consumption, which varies with tasks, settings, and software environments. Anthropic positions the new models for the most demanding technical work and continues to recommend Claude Opus 5.5 for everyday use.

The models produce output up to 30 percent faster than Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, Anthropic says. An optional fast mode for select organizations speeds up token output by up to a factor of 2.5 but costs twice as much and is available only on certain platforms, including Claude Code, the Claude Platform, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry.

Artificial Analysis’s benchmarks put Fable 5.2 clearly ahead of its rivals. On the current Index v5 at the highest compute tier, it takes first place with 65 points, five ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (60, High tier), which Google still hasn't released, six ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (59, Max tier), and a striking 15 ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, which came out only in early September.

Fable 5.2 scores best in five of nine individual tests, according to Artificial Analysis. It hits 80 percent on HLE-Diamond, a test with expert-level academic questions, 73 percent on Terminal-Bench-Science, which tests whether an AI agent can independently run scientific workflows in a terminal, and 49 percent on FrontierCode 2.0, which evaluates whether an agent can deliver useful code changes in real open-source projects.

Fable 5.2 is weaker in agentic knowledge work and terminal-based coding. It reaches 1,785 Elo on AA-Briefcase, a benchmark for multi-step knowledge work tasks, just behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 (1,813) and within the confidence interval of Opus 5.5 (1,800). On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which measures multi-step terminal tasks in areas like software development and security, it scores 60 percent, tied with Opus 5.5. Kimi K3.1 Pro (67 percent), Gemini 4 Carbon (65 percent), and Sonnet 5.5 (64 percent) rank higher here.

Peak quality comes at a price, though. Per-task costs at the highest tier average $26.50, about 2.6 times as much as Opus 5.5 ($10) and roughly double Fable 5.1 ($12.99). Fable 5.2 still scores 62 points on the Intelligence Index at the lower High and Xhigh tiers, ahead of every other model at any tier according to Artificial Analysis, while consuming far fewer tokens: 98,000 output tokens per task compared to 173,000 for Opus 5.5 at the Max tier.

The new models also set records in cybersecurity, which is seeing intense debate right now. Mythos 5.2 finds more vulnerabilities than earlier models and is better at reproducing and fixing them, Anthropic says. key_points_en: Key Development: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead just before its IPO

news.article_content_zh:
Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2 和 Mythos 5.2 在该公司 IPO 前不久重新夺回了人工智能性能领先地位，在某些情况下还大幅领先。 Opus 5.5 仍然是 Anthropic 推荐的日常使用型号。

Claude Fable 5.2 和 Claude Mythos 5.2 具有相同的模型基础，但就像它们的前辈一样，访问权限有所不同。 Fable 包含阻止网络安全和生物学中的危险任务的保护措施，并且可供所有用户使用。 Mythos 消除了其中某些限制，并且仅向通过 Anthropic 网络安全或生命科学验证计划申请的组织开放。

定价为每百万输入代币 8 美元，每百万输出代币 40 美元。至少在纸面上，这比前代产品的成本有所降低，前代产品的成本为 10 美元和 50 美元。用户实际支付的费用取决于代币消耗，而代币消耗因任务、设置和软件环境而异。 Anthropic 将新型号定位于最苛刻的技术工作，并继续推荐 Claude Opus 5.5 适合日常使用。

Anthropic 表示，这些模型的输出速度比 Fable 5.1 和 Mythos 5.1 快 30%。针对特定组织的可选快速模式可将代币输出速度提高高达 2.5 倍，但成本是其两倍，并且仅在某些平台上可用，包括 Claude Code、Claude Platform、Google Cloud 和 Microsoft Foundry。

Artificial Analysis 的基准测试显示《神鬼寓言 5.2》明显领先于其竞争对手。在当前最高计算层的 Index v5 上，它以 65 分排名第一，比 Google 尚未发布的 Gemini 4 Carbon（60，高级）领先 5 分，领先 Claude Opus 5.5（59，最高层）6 分，比 9 月初才发布的 Claude Fable 5.1 领先 15 分。

根据人工分析，《神鬼寓言 5.2》在九项单独测试中的五项中得分最高。在 HLE-Diamond（一项包含专家级学术问题的测试）上，它的得分为 80%；在 Terminal-Bench-Science（测试 AI 代理是否可以在终端中独立运行科学工作流程）上，得分为 73%；在 FrontierCode 2.0（评估代理是否可以在真正的开源项目中提供有用的代码更改）上，得分为 49%。

《神鬼寓言 5.2》在代理知识工作和基于终端的编码方面较弱。它在 AA-Briefcase（多步骤知识工作任务的基准）上达到 1,785 Elo，仅落后于 Claude Sonnet 5.5 (1,813)，并且处于 Opus 5.5 (1,800) 的置信区间内。 Terminal-Bench 4.0 衡量软件开发和安全等领域的多步骤终端任务，其得分为 60%，与 Opus 5.5 持平。 Kimi K3.1 Pro（67%）、Gemini 4 Carbon（65%）和Sonnet 5.5（64%）在这里排名更高。

不过，顶级品质是有代价的。最高级别的每任务平均成本为 26.50 美元，大约是 Opus 5.5（10 美元）的 2.6 倍，大约是 Fable 5.1（12.99 美元）的两倍。根据人工分析，《神鬼寓言 5.2》在较低的 High 和 Xhigh 级别的智力指数上仍得分 62 分，领先于任何级别的所有其他模型，同时消耗的令牌少得多：每个任务的输出令牌为 98,000 个，而 Opus 5.5 在 Max 级别的输出令牌为 173,000 个。

新模型还在网络安全方面创下了记录，目前网络安全领域引发了激烈的争论。 Anthropic 表示，Mythos 5.2 比早期模型发现了更多漏洞，并且能够更好地重现和修复这些漏洞。 Fable 是公开可用的变体，因此会阻止大多数与安全相关的任务，包括渗透测试和漏洞代码生成。 Opus 4.8 响应被阻止的网络安全请求，Opus 5 响应被阻止的生物学请求。

Anthropic 使用名为 CVE Rediscovery 的内部测试来检查在给定修复前的项目状态时，模型可以从 CVE 数据库（常见漏洞和暴露，用于对已知软件缺陷进行编目的系统）中独立找到多少已发布的漏洞。

Anthropic 表示，在 2026 年 10 月的运行中，Mythos 5.2 发现的漏洞比 Opus 5.5 多 10.2%，比 Mythos 5.1 多 14.4%，共发现 1,829 个 CVE。它在每个计算层都处于领先地位。据 Anthropic 称，一家安全公司报告称，Mythos 5.2 发现的六分之一的已确认错误已被所有其他测试的前沿模型遗漏。

Anthropic 表示，它在训练过程中故意阻止模型提高最能直接加速人工智能开发的能力，即所谓的 RSI，目前人们广泛将其视为一种风险。该公司表示，Fable 5.2 和 Mythos 5.2 在优化加速器芯片的计算内核和改进大型语言模型架构等领域的表现与 Opus 5.5 大致相当。

Anthropic 表示，代理编码、硬件开发和传统人工智能研究（包括可解释性研究）等相关功能不会受到影响。该公司表示，现在超过 90% 的更改都是由 Claude 在人...

news.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, a small AI model built for the repetitive work agents actually do
news.title_en: Meta launches Muse Ember, a small AI model built for the repetitive work agents actually do
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Meta has introduced Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient AI model to date. It's designed for the routine tasks AI agents handle all day: calling tools, handling small coding tasks, routing requests, extracting data, and processing long documents. Meta says Muse Ember delivers more intelligence per dollar at every reasoning level than Claude Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna. It costs about $0.14 per task in the Artificial Analysis test, while the larger Muse Spark 1.3 costs $2.39 for a nearly identical score of 36 versus 37. Muse Ember leads in most of Meta's own tests, but Haiku outperforms it on real coding tasks in FrontierCode 2.0-AA, scoring 34.9 percent to Muse Ember's 27.2 percent.

The model handles text, images, audio, and video and can process up to one million tokens at once. It's available now through the Meta Model API and Muse Code at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.

news.title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
news.title_en: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
Hackers are actively exploiting a recently discovered critical vulnerability that allows them to log in to privileged accounts on many Linux systems, multiple researchers are reporting.

The vulnerability, tracked under the name *sshole, arises from the interaction between OpenSSH and a code library known as musl. Linux systems that use both of these packages and meet certain other requirements can be hacked to give unauthenticated access to high-privilege accounts in a matter of seconds. *sshole became publicly known last Thursday and quickly stoked concerns it could lead to widespread compromise of Linux machines. Four days later, the prediction shows signs of becoming real.

Security firm Greynoise said Monday that honeypots it maintains in Southeast Asia have come under attack by a group it’s tracking as GT10. The group conducted “mature intrusions" into the systems, which Greynoise uses to detect attempted or successful attacks in real time. Greynoise subsequently gained access to a GT10 server that revealed potential other victims and some of the tools used in the campaign. news.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
news.title_en: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape.

Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ.

It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures.” It’s a culture war, in other words.

But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the physical consequences of its enormous appetite for electricity.

Here’s why. There are two ways to power the sort of data center that AI companies want: connecting to the grid, or generating electricity onsite. In Virginia’s Loudoun County, where data centers are ubiquitous but have been built at a steadier pace than the breakneck expansion now underway elsewhere in the country, most are connected to the existing grid.

One facility I went inside, operated by Equinix, has massive diesel generators onsite for backup but gets its power from the local utility, Dominion Energy. Much of Dominion’s electricity is generated by natural gas (which is cleaner than coal or oil, but worse than renewables).

The average data center operating in this part of Virginia today has a power capacity of 54 megawatts. That’s more than the power draw of the Denver International Airport.

Elena Schlossberg, a prominent activist against data centers in Virginia, told me she’s “always banging my head against the wall” when the industry paints the fight as a culture war. “It was always about power,” she says—that is, electricity.

Some Virginia protesters appear more animated by a broader anti-tech populism than Schlossberg, to be fair. But it’s the particular consequences of drawing so much power from the grid that have done the most to shape how the backlash has played out.

Recent protests have led to new rules from the state that data centers must pay fully for the cost of new transmission lines to the grid and make sure they’re not spread among everyone else. Data center developers told me they’re preparing for new rules that would cut them off from grid power during peak demand. news.article_content_zh:
上周，当美国各地的选民前往投票站时，我正在弗吉尼亚州阿什本，那里是世界上最大的数据中心枢纽——数据中心巷的一部分。可以说，现在席卷全国的强烈反对情绪也正是从这里开始形成的。

开车穿过它是超现实的。每条主要道路上都矗立着混凝土整体建筑，其名称包括 Skybox 和 CloudHQ。

大型科技公司普遍认为，针对数据中心的战争必须涉及比数据中心本身更大的事情。中期选举两天后，OpenAI 首席全球事务官 Chris Lehane 写道，数据中心“已经成为公众对负担能力、企业权力以及人们失去对未来的控制感到不安的代表。”换句话说，这是一场文化战争。

但在数据中心巷待了几天后，我想知道这是否真的是 Lehane 描述的代理。我确信数据中心的强烈反对更多地与电力有关，而不是大型科技公司所承认的。该行业可以改善其形象，但无法摆脱对电力的巨大需求所带来的物理后果。

原因如下。人工智能公司想要的数据中心有两种供电方式：连接到电网或现场发电。在弗吉尼亚州的劳登县，数据中心无处不在，但其建设速度比该国其他地方目前正在进行的高速扩张更为稳定，大多数数据中心都连接到现有电网。

我走进的一处设施由 Equinix 运营，现场配有大型柴油发电机作为备用，但其电力来自当地公用事业公司 Dominion Energy。多米尼恩的大部分电力由天然气发电（天然气比煤炭或石油更清洁，但比可再生能源差）。

目前，弗吉尼亚州该地区运营的数据中心的平均电力容量为 54 兆瓦。这比丹佛国际机场的耗电量还要多。

弗吉尼亚州著名的反对数据中心活动人士埃琳娜·施洛斯伯格 (Elena Schlossberg) 告诉我，当业界将这场斗争描绘成一场文化战争时，她“总是用头撞墙”。 “这总是与电力有关，”她说——也就是说，电力。

公平地说，一些弗吉尼亚州的抗议者似乎对更广泛的反科技民粹主义比施洛斯伯格更感兴趣。但正是从电网汲取如此多电力所产生的特殊后果，才最有力地塑造了强烈反对的结果。

最近的抗议活动导致该州出台了新规定，即数据中心必须全额支付通往电网的新输电线路的成本，并确保它们不会蔓延到其他地方。数据中心开发商告诉我，他们正在准备新的规则，这些规则将在高峰需求期间切断他们的电网供电。施洛斯伯格还担心电网紧张的下游影响，例如，数据中心将运行更多柴油发电机，或者多米尼恩能源公司将扩大化石燃料投入而不是可再生能源以满足需求。

该国其他地方建设的绝大多数人工智能数据中心都不是这样设计的。所需的规模是如此之大，以至于公司纷纷在几乎没有电网基础设施可连接的农村地区设立分支机构。在那里建设意味着以天然气驱动的涡轮机的形式带来自己的电力（所谓的“表后”电力）。公司还制造备用柴油发电机。例如，据报道，Anthropic 同意支付 34 亿美元购买燃气轮机，这被称为人工智能公司最大的发电采购。

即使电网就在附近，它们也不太可能满足所需的电力需求。对 AI 训练有吸引力的最小数据中心为 300 兆瓦。对于一个工业场地来说，这是很大的电力，但并非史无前例：一位数据中心开发商告诉我，他正在关注一家已经具备从电网获取这么多电力的前钢铁厂的设施。

但理想的设施更像是 6,000 兆瓦。这是芝加哥市的估计耗电量，仅该市就有 20 多个发电厂（还有数十个更远的发电厂）为该市提供电力。

数据中心公司自带电力的想法乍一看似乎很有吸引力，因为它们不会给电网带来压力。但如此规模的发电不可避免地会影响周边社区，而当公用事业建设如此规模的基础设施时，社区传统上期望对电力的去向拥有发言权。现在，私营公司正在开展类似规模的项目。

news.title: Apple’s $50 Intelligence Usage Packs extend access to some AI features
news.title_en: Apple’s $50 Intelligence Usage Packs extend access to some AI features
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Logic Pro is Apple’s first app to charge for extended usage of Apple Intelligence.﻿

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

After publishing a support article in early September outlining usage limits for some Apple Intelligence features, the company has updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for a one-time purchase price of $49.99, as spotted by 9to5Mac. It has a built-in AI assistant to do things like “start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project.”

These Intelligence Usage Packs, as Apple calls them, will allow users to continue accessing certain Apple Intelligence features that have usage limits because they rely on cloud-based AI models from OpenAI or Google Gemini. The Usage Packs can only be used by the Apple Account that purchased them (Family Sharing isn’t supported) and, as Apple explains on its website, any unused additional usage will roll over from month to month, but will expire 12 months after it was purchased.

For Logic Pro, Apple says the usage limit is “impacted by the complexity of conversations you have with the assistant.” Users finding themselves running out of access can find the option to buy an Intelligence Usage Pack in the Intelligence Features > Show Usage section of the app’s main menu. Currently, only Logic Pro has the option to buy more usage, but it’s expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers that are getting access to Apple’s AI chatbot.

news.title: Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift
news.title_en: Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Bytedance Seed introduces Seedream 5.5, a new image generation model built for professional production workflows. According to Bytedance, one improvement is stable multi-round editing across up to 100 rounds, with unchanged image areas preserved at the pixel level and no color shifts. The new Flux model also stood out here recently.

Seedream 5.5 also generates native RGBA images with transparent backgrounds, letting generated elements serve directly as design assets without manual cutouts. Bytedance says the model renders light, materials, and skin textures more realistically and reproduces dense small text more accurately.

Bytedance claims Seedream 5.5 leads models like GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst in text structure and realism. The model is gradually rolling out via Jimeng, Doubao, Doubao Work, and Volcengine Ark. A Pro version is planned.

news.title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
news.title_en: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
As a California state senator, Scott Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play a key role in setting federal AI policy.

I spoke with Wiener on Friday, only a few hours after he had been declared the victor. But he was already thinking about AI risk. The previous day, the AI nonprofit METR had released a report that had been widely interpreted as evidence that Anthropic had achieved recursive self-improvement, a phenomenon in which AI meaningfully contributes to its own advancement and AI progress potentially spins out of control.

“It’s very concerning,” Wiener said, citing the report as evidence that we are quickly running out of time to regulate AI. “It was my hope that Congress would take decisive action before [the end of] this year,” he said. “That does not appear to be happening.”

Wiener has been increasingly focused on AI in recent years, and he’s made many of the AI safety movement’s concerns his own: During our 20-minute conversation, he used the phrase “recursive self-improvement” half a dozen times, for example.“We need to slow this down,” he says. “Because it’s moving very quickly, and we could sleepwalk into a disaster.”

Wiener has already had real influence on AI policy. SB 1047, a bill that he authored in 2024, was set to become the first real piece of frontier AI legislation in the country before it was vetoed by California governor Gavin Newsom; he then sponsored SB 53, a lighter-touch bill that Newsom signed. Both bills have inspired proposed federal legislation.

Wiener’s congressional campaign received over $3 million from Public First Action, a nonprofit in favor of AI regulation that receives substantial funding from Anthropic. That contribution led opponents to criticize him for being too close to the AI industry, but Wiener says that couldn’t be further from the truth.

“Public First supported me because I was the first lawmaker in the country to introduce AI regulation and the first to pass it and get it implemented,” he wrote in a message after our interview. “The attacks on me for [Public First’s] support were shockingly cynical—literally attacking a candidate who actually regulated AI over Big Tech’s objection and falsely claiming the candidate is somehow too close to Big Tech.”

Wiener says that if Congress forms a select committee on artificial intelligence—something that Democrats have discussed since September—he’d be eager to serve. And he’s enthusiastic about many of the policy ideas floating around Congress. “I think it’s really important to have a strong, empowered, nimble federal regulator,” he says, noting that Representative Ro Khanna, a fellow Democrat from California, has proposed legislation to establish such a regulator.

He also highlights the importance of whistleblower protections, testing and auditing requirements, and a kill switch requirement, and he wants to see Congress leverage its oversight powers to hold the AI labs to account. “This is about the future of humanity, and we want to make sure that the public has a say and that the public knows what's going on,” he says.

And as a longtime state legislator, he is opposed to broad federal preemption of state AI laws, which some of the proposed federal legislation would require. “States are, as Brandeis says, laboratories,” he notes. “You want the states to be able to continue ...

news.article_content_zh:
作为加州参议员，斯科特·维纳 (Scott Wiener) 起草了旨在遏制先进人工智能风险的立法。现在，在赢得前众议院议长南希·佩洛西旧金山空缺席位的激烈国会竞选后，他可以在制定联邦人工智能政策方面发挥关键作用。

周五，就在维纳被宣布获胜几个小时后，我与他进行了交谈。但他已经在考虑人工智能的风险。前一天，人工智能非营利组织 METR 发布了一份报告，该报告被广泛解读为 Anthropic 实现了递归自我改进的证据，在这种现象中，人工智能为自身进步做出了有意义的贡献，而人工智能进步可能会失控。

“这非常令人担忧，”维纳说，并引用该报告作为证据，表明我们很快就没有时间来监管人工智能了。 “我希望国会在今年[年底]之前采取果断行动，”他说。 “这似乎并没有发生。”

近年来，维纳越来越关注人工智能，他也将人工智能安全运动的许多担忧归咎于自己：例如，在我们 20 分钟的谈话中，他六次使用了“递归自我完善”这个短语。“我们需要放慢速度，”他说。 “因为它发展得非常快，我们可能会梦游一场灾难。”

维纳已经对人工智能政策产生了真正的影响。他于 2024 年起草的 SB 1047 法案原本将成为美国第一个真正的人工智能前沿立法，但后来被加州州长 Gavin Newsom 否决；随后，他发起了 SB 53 法案，这是纽瑟姆签署的一项较为宽松的法案。这两项法案都激发了拟议的联邦立法。

维纳的国会竞选活动从 Public First Action 获得了超过 300 万美元，这是一家支持人工智能监管的非营利组织，并获得了 Anthropic 的大量资助。这一贡献导致反对者批评他与人工智能行业过于接近，但维纳表示这与事实相去甚远。

“公共优先支持我，因为我是该国第一个引入人工智能监管的立法者，也是第一个通过并实施它的立法者，”他在接受我们采访后的一条消息中写道。 “对我[公共优先]支持的攻击是令人震惊的愤世嫉俗——实际上是在攻击一位不顾大型科技公司的反对而实际上监管人工智能的候选人，并错误地声称该候选人在某种程度上与大型科技公司过于接近。”

维纳表示，如果国会成立一个人工智能特别委员会（民主党自 9 月份以来就一直在讨论这一问题），他将很乐意参与其中。他对国会提出的许多政策想法充满热情。他说：“我认为拥有一个强大、授权、灵活的联邦监管机构非常重要。”他指出，来自加州的民主党众议员罗·卡纳 (Ro Khanna) 已提议立法建立这样一个监管机构。

他还强调了举报人保护、测试和审计要求以及终止开关要求的重要性，他希望看到国会利用其监督权力让人工智能实验室承担责任。 “这关系到人类的未来，我们希望确保公众有发言权，并且公众知道正在发生什么，”他说。

作为一名长期的州立法者，他反对联邦对州人工智能法律的广泛优先权，而某些拟议的联邦立法将要求这样做。 “正如布兰迪斯所说，国家是实验室，”他指出。 “你希望各州能够继续保持灵活，而国会有时却无法做到这一点。”

维纳表示，最重要的是，他希望国会能够切实通过政策。 “至关重要的是，当国会采取行动时，我们要以真正有意义且符合当前情况的方式行事，”他说。这意味着认真对待人工智能灾难的可能性，他用人工智能安全专家通常使用的那种语言来讨论这一点。他告诉我：“就人工智能失去控制的风险而言，我们正处于一个非常危险的时刻。” “我们需要处理递归的自我完善。一旦你进入这个领域，这确实可能导致完全失控。”

他将在对抗灾难性人工智能风险方面拥有一些盟友。例如，参议员伯尼·桑德斯会见了人工智能安全运动中许多最有影响力的人物，并多次谈到人工智能和存在风险。但维纳湾区的 AGI 观点与以反对数据中心为基础的全国人工智能情绪之间仍然存在很大差距。周二，选民批准了 41 项反数据中心投票措施中的 40 项，这对于维纳和其他支持人工智能监管的人来说似乎是一个好兆头，但维纳表示，他认为这一运动更多地与当地的担忧有关，而不是与人工智能风险的更大问题有关。

“那些真正反对人工智能发展方向的人——这是他们实际上可以做点什么的领域，”他说。 “但对我来说，数据中心的抗议更多的是让人们感到不安，因为他们的社区可能会出现这样的情况，所有影响都在人们的家附近，推高了电费和用水量。据我所知，我认为这对大多数人来说是更大的问题。”

维纳称自己对国会控制人工智能的能力持“谨慎乐观”态度，因为国会在监管科技行业方面的记录不佳。他还担心美国总统唐纳德·特朗普能否通过立法，特朗普在 9 月份称对灾难性人工智能风险的担忧是“骗局”，并表现出完全不愿意与中国合作，而维纳认为这对于防止人工智能最严重后果至关重要。

celebrity.full_text_en:
one of the more interesting developments in the ai agent economy is agents hiring other agents to get work done.

@termix_ai recently showcased this through Montage Studio on https://t.co/9ReKMK2L7m.

here's how it works.

you submit a video production brief. Montage Studio breaks it into smaller jobs and hires specialized agents to handle the storyboard, video rendering and music.

it then coordinates their work, combines the results and delivers the finished video.

each job goes through escrow on TermiX.

this shows how agents can take responsibility for larger tasks, outsource specialized work and pay other agents for their contributions.

but this requires more than communication. agents need to discover services, agree on prices, secure payments, verify delivery and handle disputes.

that's where TermiX's Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP) comes in.

its workflow brings the process together:

escrow → delivery → challenge → settlement.

with TermiX Skills, agents can also connect to the marketplace, find work and participate in these transactions.

the direction is clear: agents are moving beyond isolated tasks towards hiring, coordinating and paying other agents to complete larger jobs.

that's the kind of autonomous economy TermiX is building towards.

when agents start doing business with each other, reliable transaction infrastructure becomes essential.

#TermiX #AACP
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理经济中最有趣的发展之一是代理雇佣其他代理来完成工作。

@termix_ai 最近通过 Montage Studio 在 上展示了这一点。

这是它的工作原理。

您提交视频制作简介。 Montage Studio 将其分解为更小的工作，并聘请专门的代理来处理故事板、视频渲染和音乐。

然后，它协调他们的工作，合并结果并交付完成的视频。

每个作业都经过 TermiX 上的托管。

这表明代理人如何承担更大的任务，外包专门工作并支付其他代理人的贡献。

但这需要的不仅仅是沟通。代理商需要发现服务、商定价格、确保付款、验证交付和处理纠纷。

这就是 TermiX 的代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 的用武之地。

其工作流程将流程整合在一起：

托管→交付→质疑→结算。

借助 TermiX Skills，代理商还可以连接到市场、寻找工作并参与这些交易。

方向很明确：代理商正在超越孤立的任务，转向雇用、协调和支付其他代理商来完成更大的工作。

这就是 TermiX 正在建设的自主经济。

当代理商开始相互开展业务时，可靠的交易基础设施就变得至关重要。

#TermiX #AACP

celebrity.full_text_en:
telling an AI agent what it shouldn't do is different from making it technically unable to do it.

when an AI agent is handling someone's money, that difference matters.

you can tell an agent to avoid certain assets, set a spending limit or stop trading after a certain loss. but if it still has broad permission to execute transactions, those instructions only go so far.

with MOTES (@meetmotes), the owner sets the mandate and signs the permissions. before a proposed transaction goes through, the smart account checks it against the rules the owner approved.

so the agent can still analyse the market and come up with strategies, but it has to work within those limits. it can't just give itself permission to spend more or trade assets outside the approved list.

i think this is a better foundation for autonomous finance. giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. making sure it only has the authority the owner gave it is just as important.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
告诉人工智能代理它不应该做什么与​​使其在技术上无法做到这一点是不同的。

当人工智能代理处理某人的资金时，这种差异很重要。

您可以告诉代理人避免某些资产、设置支出限额或在出现一定损失后停止交易。但如果它仍然拥有执行交易的广泛权限，那么这些指令就只能到此为止。

通过 MOTES (@meetmotes)，所有者可以设置授权并签署权限。在拟议的交易进行之前，智能账户会根据所有者批准的规则对其进行检查。

因此，代理仍然可以分析市场并制定策略，但它必须在这些限制内运作。它不能只是允许自己在批准的清单之外支出更多资金或交易资产。

我认为这是自主金融更好的基础。赋予代理人做出决策的能力是一回事。确保它仅具有所有者授予的权限也同样重要。

celebrity.full_text_en:
A user discovered a hidden chip in an off-brand power bank purchased in Guangzhou using Claude Code.

Every time it charged an iPhone, it secretly copied the entire phone's data. It also read Wi-Fi passwords, connected to the home network, and sent all the information to a remote server.

This power bank was bought at the airport three weeks ago for $19, labeled as 30,000 mAh, hefty with no brand name.

When first plugged in, the screen prompted "Trust This Computer," and the user clicked trust without thinking, granting it one-click access to read all data.

This morning, after setting up Claude Code to monitor file reads, the screen flashed yellow and red warnings just 10 seconds into charging—data was being transmitted.

The power bank was identified as a mini-computer with built-in 64 GB storage and network connectivity.

Regular charging cables only use power lines, but this one uses both power and data lines, and it has already copied:

→ Device info, 1,206 contacts
→ All apps including 2 banking apps
→ 3,912 photos including passport
→ Wi-Fi network names and keys
→ Wife's iPhone photos

Every charge, it uses the key to go online and send new data—19 uploads over 3 weeks, last one at 2:14 AM last night.

The user immediately unplugged it, used Claude Code to block that IP, and changed the Wi-Fi password and banking app logins.

A repair shop took it apart for a look—details below. Suggestion: Check every power bank in your home today.

the real test for an agent marketplace is not how many agents it lists. it's whether people and agents can successfully hire them.

celebrity.full_text_en:
China cracked recursive self-improvement 🤯

Tencent dropped 27B model that rewrites, retrains, and refines itself.. with zero human in the loop.

It’s called "Terminal-RSI" and it solves one of the biggest problems with AI.

They are incredibly lazy.

Usually, an agent will make partial progress, claim it succeeded, and completely fail the final environment verifier check. this new pipeline forces agents to actually finish the job.

here’s how it works:

they built a recursive loop with two alternating phases..

- RSR (recursive self-rewrite): the model fine-tunes itself on its own successfully rewritten trajectories

- RPR (recursive policy-refine): it then runs reinforcement learning (ppo) using a "critic" inherited directly from the previous stage to lock in those discovered behaviors

- Loop: the training sequence leapfrogs itself: Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

and the numbers are insane..

they applied this to a qwen3.8-27b base model. across the four "terminal-bench" suites, the agent's average success rate jumped from 20.68% all the way to 50.58%.

on the absolute hardest benchmark suite (terminal-bench 4.0), the base model scored a flat 0.00%.

after terminal-rsi?

it hit 19.84% (putting it right on par with reference models like gemini 3.8 flash).

the secret sauce? they fixed the reward system.

instead of giving the ai "dense rewards" for just trying or passing semantic checks, they switched to a "success-prioritized reward" (spr).

it mathematically separates strict success from partial credit.

basically, the agent only gets the massive reward payout if the code actually passes the final terminal gate.. so it stops faking success.

the gap between partial local repairs and strict terminal verification is closing fast.

we are watching agents build their own training environments and level up autonomously.. the future is wild.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
中国破解了递归自我完善🤯

腾讯放弃了重写、重新训练和完善自身的 27B 模型……循环中零人力。

它被称为“Terminal-RSI”，它解决了人工智能最大的问题之一。

他们非常懒惰。

通常，代理会取得部分进展，声称已成功，但最终环境验证程序检查完全失败。这条新管道迫使特工真正完成工作。

它的工作原理如下：

他们建立了一个具有两个交替阶段的递归循环。

- RSR（递归自重写）：模型根据自己成功重写的轨迹进行自我微调

- RPR（递归策略细化）：然后使用直接从前一阶段继承的“批评家”来运行强化学习（ppo），以锁定那些发现的行为

- 循环：训练序列自行跳跃：Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

而且数字很疯狂..

他们将其应用于 qwen3.8-27b 基础模型。在四个“终端替补”套件中，特工的平均成功率从 20.68% 一路跃升至 50.58%。

在绝对最难的基准测试套件（terminal-bench 4.0）上，基本模型的得分为 0.00%。

在终端 rsi 之后？

它达到了 19.84%（与 Gemini 3.8 flash 等参考型号相当）。

秘密武器？他们确定了奖励制度。

他们不再为人工智能尝试或通过语义检查而给予“密集奖励”，而是转向“成功优先奖励”（spr）。

它在数学上将严格的成功与部分的功劳区分开来。

基本上，只有当代码实际上通过了最终的终端门时，代理才会获得巨额奖励。因此它不再假装成功。

部分本地修复和严格的终端验证之间的差距正在迅速缩小。

我们正在观察代理建立自己的培训环境并自主升级......未来是疯狂的。

celebrity.full_text_en:
i killed the infographics show with 1 claude opus prompt

now i made a full 10 minute story video in full code

this cost me $0 in ai video generations btw

turned it into a prompt you can use for free and make any topic u want, enjoy ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for my topic and my script. If I have no script, write one from my topic.
Ask which image model I have: GPT Image 2, or any model that takes reference images at 2K-4K, at about $0.03-0.05 an image.
Ask which voice I have: ElevenLabs, or Kokoro for free.
Before generating everything, show me a look test: one plate, one character sheet cut out and rigged, and a 10 s shot with typing, a tag and a character who talks and points. Wait for my OK.
</inputs>

<look>
A 1920x1080 animated explainer in the style of the big flat-vector infographic channels.
- Every line of narration is acted out by cartoon people inside a full illustrated place.
- All motion is code. There are no AI video generations, just a few still images that code cuts up, rigs and animates.

Art:
- Flat colour shapes with NO outlines, at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes and crisp edges.
- Muted palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple. Salmon-pink skin, big round heads, dot eyes, small bodies.
- Mood comes from the plate's own light: daylight, a cold blue night, warm indoor lamps.

Code colours:
- ink #2b2d42, red #d62828, orange #f4a261, gold #f6b93b, green #2fb37a, navy #1f2a48
- headline tomato #e2552f and purple #5b3fa6
- grey labels #8a8c9c, white cards #ffffff
- Font: Montserrat 800-900 (Google Fonts), all caps on cards and signs.

Pace:
- A new place every 3-4 s, about 10 places a minute.
- Something new arrives every 2 s: a tag, a stamp, a person walking in, a number.
- Never hold a still over 1 s. Never have a character who doesn't move.

Banned:
- outlines, glossy UI panels floating over the art, emoji, burned-in subtitles
- any channel's logo or name, photos of real people
- facts written on a plain colour card when the place could hold them
</look>

<art>
About 60 images in all ($2-3).

Every prompt starts with this style core, word for word:
"Flat vector illustration in exactly the same art style as the reference images: NO outlines or line art anywhere, every shape is a flat solid colour fill with at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes, crisp clean edges, no gradients, no texture, no painterly lighting. Muted modern palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple, salmon-pink skin. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos."

Then add one line that locks the setting ("The setting is [time, place]: [materials, light sources], nothing from other eras unless asked"). Feed 3-5 frames of a reference channel in as style references, with their logo cropped off.

1. Hero plates, about 24, one full 16:9 image each, for places you zoom into or come back to.
   - EMPTY: "no people, no characters, no animals".
   - Straight-on, with an open floor in the middle where characters will stand.
   - Blank signs, boards, screens and pages that code writes on later.
2. Quad plates, about 19, giving 76 more places. Pack 4 places into one image:
   "The image is a 2x2 grid of FOUR completely separate scenes, each filling exactly one quarter of the image (each quarter is itself a 16:9 picture), divided by perfectly straight thin pure-white gutters, one vertical down the exact centre and one horizontal across the exact centre."
   - Then describe the TOP-LEFT, TOP-RIGHT, BOTTOM-LEFT and BOTTOM-RIGHT scenes.
   - Split each quad on the brightest white row and column near the centre, walk out while the line stays over 60% white, and trim 6 px more.
   - Crop each tile to 16:9 at 1920x1080.
   - Object close-ups make great tiles: a desk, a screen, a document, a plate of food, a vault.
3. Main characters, 2-3 of them. Write one fixed description per character (age, hair, face, every piece of clothing with colours) and paste it word for word into every sheet.
   - Base sheet: 6 views. (1) front, neutral, drawn WITHOUT ARMS, only round smooth shoulder sockets where the arms would join; (2) the same armless front with a second emotion; (3) side view walking right; (4) seen from behind; (5) and (6) two poses the script needs.
   - Expression sheet: 6 armless fronts (hopeful, disgusted, terrified, exhausted, sick, shocked, or whatever the script needs), with the base sheet as a reference.
   - Pose sheet: 6 full poses with their props (sitting at a desk typing, sleeping, eating, running, signing, falling), with the base sheet as a reference.
4. Everyone else: role sheets of 4-6 people, each drawn in the exact pose their shot needs; crowd sheets of 8-10 small figures; prop sheets.
   - Every sheet: "on a solid flat chroma green background (#00B140) with lots of empty green space between figures; nothing touches, nothing on any character or object is green, full bodies, nothing cut off by the edges".
5. Thumbnail art: the same characters with richer saturated cartoon lighting and extreme emotions, the top quarter left free, no text, with the base sheets as references.
</art>

<rig>
Cutouts:
- The background is every border-connected pixel with G - max(R,B) over 40 and within 110 of the median green. Key only from the border, or dark clothes leak.
- Add a 2 px soft alpha band and clamp G to max(R,B) + 6 inside it, which kills the green fringe.
- Group the pieces by figure and drop specks. Name every sprite, and show me a named contact sheet.

Armless front figures become puppets:
- Split the head at the neck: the narrowest alpha row under the head.
- Find both shoulder sockets and the eye boxes.
- Inpaint the hole under the head from the body's own colours, so a nod never shows a gap.
- Write everything to rig.js: size, neck, sockets, eye boxes, skin RGB, sleeve RGB.
- Arms: upper L1 about 0.13 of the figure's height, lower L2 about 0.12, thickness about 0.04. Use sleeve colour to the elbow and skin for the forearm, a 0.82x darker sleeve when the arm is behind the body, and round caps and joins.
- Hands: mittens in three shapes (mitt, open, fist), plus a point with one finger out.
- Arm poses: each is a hand target relative to its shoulder, in units of L = L1 + L2, solved by two-bone IK (where there are two signs, the first is the left arm).
  - down: (∓0.04, 0.97)
  - rest: (±0.1, 0.9)
  - hips: (∓0.42, 0.55) with fists
  - point: right hand to (0.86, -0.32)
  - present: right hand to (0.75, 0.25), open
  - shrug: (∓0.62, 0.12), open
  - up: (∓0.32, -0.9)
  - hands on head
  - chin: a fist at the neck
  - hold: (±0.42, 0.45)
  - wave: (0.5, -0.75)
  - stop: (0.55, -0.1)
  - cheer: (∓0.55, -0.75) with fists
  - A pose change blends the two targets over 0.3-0.5 s with ease-in-out.
- Side, back and pose sprites stay whole images. Only the head turns, and a drawing or typing hand jitters ±6 px.
</rig>

<animation>
One HTML canvas where every frame is a pure function of time t: window .seek(t), READY, END, and EV, a list of sound events by name.
- Hang every shot on the narration: S('exact words', fn) starts a shot 0.08 s before that phrase. Repeated words are looked up by occurrence number.
- One function per shot, one shots file per chapter.

Motion primitives (Δ = t - start):
- pop: 0.3 s back-ease overshoot, 1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2.
- spring in: 1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ).
- kick on impact: 1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ).
- shake: x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ), y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ).
- Exits shrink with ease-in over 0.25 s. Things arrive with a spring, a squash or a white puff, never a plain fade.

Camera:
- camP(plate, zoom, fx, fy) keeps the view inside the plate's edges.
- Every shot moves from one [zoom, fx, fy] to another with ease-in-out, a 2-4% push or a slow pan, so nothing holds still.
- Draw the plate and everything on it inside the same camera transform.
- Keep zoom under 1.33x on quad tiles. Zoom deeper only on hero plates.

Transitions:
- Push: the old shot slides out left while the new one slides in from the right, 0.24 s ease-in-out, with a whoosh 0.02 s before.
- Chapter splat: a #f4f1fb blob covers the screen in 0.2 s and clears in 0.2 s. It's a 1,250 px circle, 12 big satellite blobs at golden-angle spacing and 10 small droplets further out, shifted 120 px left on the way in and 140 px right on the way out.

Characters, alive in every frame:
- Breathing: scale 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t).
- Head nod: 0.025 sin(2.1t) rad, or 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t) while that character's line is spoken.
- Blink: every 2.7-4.2 s, seeded per figure. For 0.14 s, paint each eye box over in skin colour with a curved lash line.
- Walk:
  - Bob |sin| at 2.2% of the figure's height, with a body rock of ±0.035 rad.
  - Side-view walk sprites slide 1.5 leg lengths per step cycle, so the feet don't skate.
- Enter on the spring, sometimes with a hop. Fear is a fast shake (sin 70t). Surprise is a jump and an orange "!".
- A soft contact shadow ellipse under every figure. Night shots darken them with brightness(1 - k), so they match the plate.
- Every character on screen acts on its line: points at the thing being named, presents it, shrugs, cheers, holds its head.
</animation>

<graphics>
Text only lives on things in the world, typed letter by letter: 28 letters a second (34 for short tags). Each letter starts 1.45x big and 0.7 em to the right and settles in 0.18 s with ease-out.

The full kit:
- Board: a white rounded board (radius 20) that drops 420 px on the spring and swings 0.25 rad into place, or stands on a wooden post and swings up from -1 rad.
  - Soft drop shadow (blur 22, y 8, 22%) and a faint darker strip along its bottom edge.
  - Lines typed 0.3 s apart.
- Date card: top left at (70, 70), white, 120 px tall, at least 330 px wide, radius 18. An orange calendar icon, a grey "DATE:" at 26 px, the date typed at 44 px weight 900. Pops in over 0.32 s.
- Place card: the same card with a red map pin and "PLACE:".
- Tag: a 6 px line with a dot at the thing, drawn in 0.2 s, then a rounded pill (the text at 40 px weight 900) pops on its end. Ink, red, gold or orange pills.
- Number card: a white card with a small grey label and a big red number. Long numbers roll up like a counter with ease-out.
- Red X: two round 30 px strokes, 0.11 s each, 0.01 s apart, with a soft shadow. One goes over every wrong idea.
- Stamp: red text in a double rounded border, tilted -0.12 rad. It slams from 2.1x to 1x in 0.14 s, then kicks.
- Banner: a full-width headline band, 92 px white caps on tomato or purple, rotated -0.02 rad, sliding in from the left over 0.22 s.
- Speech bubble: white, radius 36, with a tail. Thought cloud: a pill with two small circles.
- Orange "?" that bobs and sways over a puzzled head, and an orange "!" pop.
- White puff and poof clouds, speed lines, light blue sweat drops, coins and bills, a soft vignette, and a colour tint for mood.
- Write on the plate's own blank boards, screens and pages whenever the place has them. Measure the blank's rectangle on a grid overlay of the plate first.
</graphics>

<voice>
- ElevenLabs: a deep, warm US documentary narrator, eleven_v4, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0, speaker boost, with the timestamps endpoint.
- About 170-180 words a minute, using the voice's own speed setting (1.0-1.1). Never speed it up with atempo: it sounds chipmunked.
- Long scripts go in 3 chunks split at chapter breaks, passing the previous and next text so the read stays continuous.
- Cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, leave 0.5 s at chapter breaks, and add a 0.3 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the alignment into words.js.
- Run faster-whisper over the result and diff it against the script before building the picture.
- Free route: Kokoro, then faster-whisper for the word times.
</voice>

<sound>
- Music: 2-3 free documentary beds from Pixabay, crossfaded over 3 s at big beats.
- Duck the music under the voice (30 ms attack, 0.3 s hold, 0.45 s release) and let it swell back up between chapters.
- SFX from Mixkit, one per event, aligned by their peaks, 6 dB quieter on speech: a typewriter tick on typing, a whoosh on pushes and splats, a pop on tags and cards, a thud on stamps, a hit on every red X, a ding on ticks, plus sounds that fit the scene.
- Gate: during speech the voice sits 15+ dB over music plus SFX (median of 100 ms frames), and the background is louder than the voice in under 1% of frames.
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dB.
</sound>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Order:
   - the look test
   - the art in batches, with a contact sheet after each
   - cutouts and rig
   - voice and word times
   - shots, chapter by chapter
3. Check before any full render: a contact sheet per chapter, one frame every 2 s. Fix:
   - empty or overflowing signs
   - text over a face
   - black plate edges
   - feet floating off the floor
   - two shots in a row in the same place
   - any 4 s where nothing new arrives
4. Render at 30 fps, 4 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, frames piped to libx264 CRF 16-18.
   - Split long videos across 4-6 parallel browser pages and join the parts.
   - Scan the result for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Too few places reads as lazy. One plate held for 30 s with cards over it looks cheap. Budget about 10 new places a minute.
- Some image models ignore "no arms". GPT Image 2 follows it.
- Paste the same character description into every sheet and feed the base sheet back in, or faces and clothes drift.
- Quad tiles are only about 1920 px wide. Pushing past 1.33x looks soft.
- Plates with people already drawn in can't be animated. Ask for EMPTY and check before cutting.
- Text on a card floating over the art looks like a slideshow. Write on the world.
- Long renders crash. Render in parts you can rerun, and back up the shot files before every big patch.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, my script, my image model and my voice, then make the look test.
</start>

<看>
大型平面矢量信息图表频道风格的 1920x1080 动画讲解器。
- 每一行叙述都由卡通人物在一个充满插图的地方表演。
- 所有的动作都是代码。没有人工智能视频生成，只有一些经过代码切割、装配和动画处理的静态图像。

艺术：
- 没有轮廓的扁平颜色形状，最多一种稍暗的扁平色调，简单的几何形状和清晰的边缘。
- 柔和的调色板：灰蓝灰色、板岩青色、暖米色、海军蓝、柔和的紫色。鲑鱼粉色的皮肤，圆圆的大脑袋，圆点的眼睛，小小的身体。
- 情绪来自于盘子本身的光线：日光、寒冷的蓝色夜晚、温暖的室内灯光。

代码颜色：
- 墨水 #2b2d42、红色 #d62828、橙色 #f4a261、金色 #f6b93b、绿色 #2fb37a、海军蓝 #1f2a48
- 标题番茄#e2552f 和紫色#5b3fa6
- 灰色标签#8a8c9c，白色卡片#ffffff
- 字体：Montserrat 800-900（Google 字体），卡片和标志上全部大写。

步速：
- 每 3-4 秒一个新位置，每分钟大约 10 个位置。
- 每 2 秒就会有新的东西到达：标签、邮票、走进来的人、号码。
- 切勿保持静止超过 1 秒。永远不要有不动的角色。

禁止：
- 轮廓、漂浮在艺术上方的光滑 UI 面板、表情符号、内置字幕
- 任何频道的标志或名称、真人照片
- 当地方可以容纳时，将事实写在普通彩色卡片上
</看>

<艺术>
总共大约 60 张图片（2-3 美元）。

每个提示都以这种风格核心开头，逐字逐句：
“平面矢量插图的艺术风格与参考图像完全相同：任何地方都没有轮廓或线条艺术，每个形状都是平面纯色填充，最多有一个稍暗的平面阴影作为形式，简单的几何形状，清晰干净的边缘，没有渐变，没有纹理，没有绘画照明。柔和的现代调色板：灰蓝色，板岩青色，温暖米色，海军蓝，柔和的紫色，鲑鱼粉红色皮肤。没有文字，没有字母，没有数字，没有徽标。”

然后添加一行来锁定设置（“设置是[时间，地点]：[材料，光源]，除非询问，否则没有其他时代的内容”）。将参考通道的 3-5 帧作为样式参考，并剪掉其徽标。
